turns.text:
The sky is blue because of the way light interacts with it. Light travels in straight lines, but as we look into the atmosphere around us, our eyes can see that light is bent by refraction and diffraction. This causes the different colors to bend or refract (curl) at different angles, creating a spectrum of light that we can see.

The sky appears blue because it reflects some of this light back from the earth, which makes the sky appear blue to us. This is why the sky looks blue when viewed through a telescope.
